mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: The potential for damaging winds will continue through late afternoon across the lower Mississippi River Valley

details.label: Summary
details.text: The potential for damaging winds will continue through late afternoon across the lower Mississippi River Valley

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Regional radar imagery out of southern MS and eastern LA depicts poorly organized, and largely outflow-dominant, convection. These cells/clusters have been producing occasionally strong downbursts with velocity data depicting 40-50 knot outflow within the lowest 1-2 kft ARL. Additionally, surface stations that have been impacted by outflow have reported temperature reductions on the order of 20 F. Given these conditions within the convective cold pools and weak low-level shear sampled by regional VWPs, outflow boundaries should become more prominent within the next hour or so. Boundary collisions downstream across east/southeast LA will likely promote additional updraft development within a hot and unstable air mass (characterized by low-level lapse rates approaching 9 C/km and MLCAPE estimated to be around 2500-3000 J/kg). Intense downbursts will be possible with the more vigorous updraft pulses as additional convection develops and spreads south into this air mass over the next few hours. Given the thermodynamic conditions, embedded swaths of 45-60 mph appear possible within the strongest downbursts

details.label: Most probable threats
details.text: MOST PROBABLE PEAK WIND GUST...UP TO 60 MPH
